narrative:
The model determined that you have a 63% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This likelihood crossed the threshold the bank uses to approve loans, which is why your application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the amount you requested, and the duration of the loan. Your checking account status had the greatest impact and pushed the decision firmly toward rejection. Having a negative balance (under 0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants—only about 13% of them show this status—whereas most approved borrowers have either no checking account or a positive balance. This signaled higher risk to the model.

The loan amount you requested worked in your favor. At 1,659 DM it was well below the average of roughly 3,020 DM seen among approved applications, which helped pull the prediction toward approval. However, this positive effect was not strong enough to overcome the other factors.

The requested duration of 24 months also worked against you. Approved loans average closer to 19 months, so the longer repayment period increased the perceived risk.

Taken together, these elements led the model to conclude that the risk was too high. To improve your chances on a future application, focus first on bringing your checking account balance into positive territory and consider requesting a shorter loan term or a smaller amount if possible. Addressing these areas should meaningfully improve how a similar model evaluates your profile. (248 words)
